history.summary: Built by the Singhania family's JK Trust (formed 1953) and opened to the public in 1960; the temple's origin is traced to a dream of Ram Pyari Devi, wife of Lala Kamlapat Singhania, in which Lord Krishna blessed her. A blend of ancient and modern architecture in white marble and sandstone with a high-ventilated mandapa; five shrines — central Radha-Krishna, plus Lakshminarayan, Ardhanarishvara, Narmadeshwar and Hanuman — set in a triangular campus with three ponds and manicured gardens. Maintained by the JK Trust. Photography is prohibited inside; security frisking at entry.

name: J.K. Temple (Radhakrishna Temple)
town_description: Major industrial city on the south bank of the Ganga, ~80 km west of Lucknow; the 'industrial capital' of Uttar Pradesh, with Kanpur Central as a major railway hub on the Delhi–Howrah corridor.

travel.airport: Kanpur Airport (Chakeri), ~14 km; Lucknow (CCS International), ~80 km
travel.road: First Street, Sarvodaya Nagar; near Moti Jheel; on city bus/auto routes from Kanpur Central

visitor_information.best_time: October–March; Janmashtami and Diwali draw large crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM – 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM – 9:00 PM; one source cites 9:00 AM – 12:00 noon and 4:00 – 6:30 PM (conflict — verify)
